The Independent National Electoral Commission has said it is fully prepared for the forthcoming election, disclosing that it has added 57,000 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System machines to ensure the immediate replacement of faulty devices during the exercise.
The commission’s representative, Ike Nnenna, disclosed on this on Friday while speaking at an electoral literacy programme organised by CHAMP Initiative in partnership with the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre, and the European Union in Abuja.
Nnenna said the commission had put adequate measures in place to address possible technological challenges and was also prepared in terms of logistics.
“INEC is very prepared for the election in terms of electronic. We have added 57,000 BVAS to make sure that any BVAS malfunctioning is immediately replaced,” she said.
She added, “In terms of logistics, we are very prepared for the election.”
The INEC representative, who said she was impressed by the level of participation he witnessed at the programme, however, expressed concern that some students did not have Permanent Voter Cards.
She urged the students to obtain their PVCs and participate actively in the electoral process, while advising them to avoid actions that could lead to trouble during elections.
Also speaking, the Team Lead of CHAMP Initiative, Christopher Olusa, urged students and other young people to make informed decisions when voting, rather than choosing candidates spontaneously on election day.
He said young people should study candidates, their campaigns and political ideologies ahead of the forthcoming general election.
“One of the major things I will talk about is that students must make informed voting decisions. During the mock elections, decisions were made on the spot. However, when it comes to a general election, especially the one coming up next, students and young people should already know who they want to vote for,” Olusa said.
He said voting decisions should be based on issues, campaigns and voters’ convictions about candidates and political parties.
Olusa added that the votes cast by young people would determine their future, urging them to understand the implications of their electoral choices.
On the responsibilities of the campus ambassadors inaugurated through the programme, he said they would sustain electoral awareness activities in their respective institutions beyond the event.
“The campus ambassadors will be the representatives of the programme after today’s event. They are the ones who will champion other activities that we will be carrying out on campus because this programme is not going to be a one-off event,” he said.
He explained that the ambassadors would organise engagements within their campuses, promote the objectives of the initiative and encourage continuous participation among students.
Olusa also called on INEC to earn the confidence of young Nigerians, noting that the commission’s performance would have significant implications for the country’s leadership and the future of the youth.
“We want to trust INEC. We want to trust them, and we want to hope that they will deliver on their mandate of delivering free, fair, credible, and peaceful elections,” he said.
He urged young people to have confidence in the electoral process, stressing that credible elections were essential to ensuring accountable leadership and governance.
